Does this happen in 0.3.0 ?

Maybe `nvim_command()` should not trigger swap at all?  This is a similar question as https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/5486 . 

OTOH you could just use

    :call nvim_command('noswap edit foo')
This sounds like https://github.com/vim/vim/issues/3221 and bisecting shows that it _was_ introduced by b7514493.

issue.title: confirm doesn't show options when used with autocmd's

labels.name: bug-regression
labels.description: wrong behavior that was introduced in a previous commit (please bisect)

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
<!-- Before reporting: search existing issues and check the FAQ. -->

- `nvim --version`: 0.3.1
- Operating system/version: Arch
- Terminal name/version: alacritty 0.1.0
- `$TERM`: screen-256color 

### Steps to reproduce using

```
cat > test-init.vim <<HERE
autocmd BufNewFile * call confirm('test')
HERE
```
```
nvim -u test-init.vim

```

run the following command
```
:e myfile.we
```

### Actual behaviour

Nothing seems to happen. File doesn't open. No confirm dialog is displayed but, if you hit enter you will go to the file. Seems that confirm is working but not being visually displayed.

### Expected behaviour
I expected to see a confirm dialog at the bottom of the screen, like if I ran the following by itself (which does work)
```
:call confirm('test')
```

Appreciate you people for looking into this :)
